When an application starts, the default spatial container opens first to display the application's initial interface. Additionally, you can use the PICO Spatial SDK to open or close a spatial container.
## Open a WindowContainer
You can open a WindowContainer in the following two ways:

* Use `Context`:
   ```Kotlin
   val context = LocalContext.current // Create a context (or use other methods to obtain the context you want)
   context.openWindowContainer(id: String, tag: String? = null, bundle: Bundle? = null)
   ```

* Use `SpatialNavigator` (a class provided by the PICO Spatial SDK specifically for opening and closing spatial containers):
   ```Kotlin
   val spatialNavigator = LocalSpatialNavigator.current // Create a SpatialNavigator
   spatialNavigator.openWindowContainer(id: String, tag: String? = null, bundle: Bundle? = null)
   ```


If you need to precisely close a specific WindowContainer in the future, specify the `tag` parameter when calling `openWindowContainer`.

The parameter descriptions are as follows:
| **Parameter** | **Required** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | Yes | The WindowContainer's name. |
| tag | No | The custom tag attached to the WindowContainer when it is opened. <br>  <br> * If `openWindowContainer` is called with the same `id` and `tag == null`, it operates in "new" mode, meaning a new WindowContainer is opened each time. <br> * If `openWindowContainer` is called with the same `id` and `tag != null`, it operates in "reuse" mode. That is, after the window is created for the first time, each subsequent call to `openWindowContainer` will bring the original window to the foreground. |
| bundle | No | Custom passthrough data, which can be obtained at the root node of the WindowContainer's content. |

For example, if you want to treat the title of `NewsContent` as data and pass it to its WindowContainer when opening it, you can follow these steps:

1. When registering a WindowContainer named "NewsWindow", retrieve a bundle for the root node of its content.
   ```Kotlin
   WindowContainer(
       id = "NewsWindow",
       form = Form.IN_VOLUME,
       resizeType = ContainerResizeType.ContentMinSize,
       size = ContainerSize(defaultWidth = 1280.dp, defaultHeight = 720.dp),
       enableMaterialBackground = false
   ) {
       NewsContent(this.bundle)
   }
   ```

2. When opening the WindowContainer named "NewsWindow", convert the title into a parameter to be passed in the bundle.
   ```Kotlin
   @Composable 
   fun OpenWindowContainerSample() { 
       val spatialNavigator = LocalSpatialNavigator.current
       val newsTitle = "\uD83D\uDDBC\uFE0F 2D & 3D Content Layout \uD83D\uDDFF"
       PicoTheme {
           Button( 
               onClick = {
                   spatialNavigator.openWindowContainer(
                       "NewsWindow",
                       "news-1",
                       Bundle().apply { putString("TITLE", newsTitle) }) 
               }
           ) {
               Text( 
                   text = "Open News Window", 
                   fontSize = 28.sp, 
                   fontFamily = FontFamily.Serif, 
               ) 
           }
       }
   } 
   ```

3. In `NewsContent`, retrieve and use data via the bundle.
   ```Kotlin
   @Composable 
   fun NewsContent(bundle: Bundle? = null) { 
       val newsTitle = bundle?.getString("TITLE") ?: "Fail to pass in data!"
       PicoTheme {
           Column( 
               modifier = Modifier 
                   .fillMaxSize() 
                   .background( 
                       color = PicoTheme.colorScheme.accent.copy(alpha = 0.9f), 
                       shape = RoundedCornerShape(60.dp) 
                   ) 
                   .padding(vertical = 30.dp, horizontal = 30.dp), 
               horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally, 
               verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(30.dp), 
           ) {
               Text( 
                   text = newsTitle, 
                   color = PicoTheme.colorScheme.onAccent, 
                   fontSize = 50.sp, 
                   fontFamily = FontFamily.Serif 
               ) 
               // Other content...
           } 
       } 
   } 
   ```


## Close a WindowContainer
You can close a WindowContainer via `Context` or `SpatialNavigator`.
```Kotlin
// Close the current WindowContainer
// The current WindowContainer can only be closed by SpatialNavigator
spatialNavigator.closeWindowContainer()

// Batch close WindowContainers with the same name
context.closeWindowContainer(id)
// or
spatialNavigator.closeWindowContainer(id)

// Precisely close a WindowContainer whose tag is not null when it is opened
context.closeWindowContainer(id, tag)
// or
spatialNavigator.closeWindowContainer(id, tag)
```

Code sample:
```Kotlin
@Composable
fun CloseWindowContainerSample(bundle: Bundle?) {
    val spatialNavigator = LocalSpatialNavigator.current
    Column {
        Button(onClick = {
            // Close the WindowContainer named "myUniqueWindow" that was opened with tag "unique"
            spatialNavigator.closeWindowContainer(id = "myUniqueWindow", tag = "unique")
        }) {
            Text("Close WindowContainers with same name")
        }
        Button(onClick = {
            // Close all WindowContainers named "myWindow"
            spatialNavigator.closeWindowContainer(id = "myWindow")
        }) {
            Text("Close WindowContainers with same name")
        }
        Button(onClick = {
            // Close the current WindowContainer
            spatialNavigator.closeWindowContainer()
        }) {
            Text("Close current WindowContainer")
        }
    }
}
```
